caption.text: \caption{\textbf{In CIFAR-5m networks, InfoNCE and spectral learners disagree on order as well as geometry, and a monotone link explains little beyond an affine map.} (a)~Discrepancy over the tolerance of each criterion; Theorem~\ref{thm:link} predicts agreement below the horizontal line, and the exact link of the theorem shows this pattern. (b)~Density of kernel entries of one pair of runs. (c)~Share of the squared-distance discrepancy explained by successive maps, with the share required by the preregistered prediction. Marks in (a) and~(c) are medians over pairs. Figure~\ref{fig:app-s21} gives both sample sizes.}

caption_v7_archived.text: \caption{\textbf{Inside the premises of Theorem~\ref{thm:link}, InfoNCE and spectral learners agree on order and differ in geometry by its link, whereas CIFAR-5m networks disagree even on order.} (a)~Share of pairs of runs with the same global order $T_E$. (b,~e)~Kernel entries of one pair of runs. (c)~Largest difference of mean-normalized distances. (d)~Discrepancy over the tolerance of each criterion; the theorem predicts agreement below the horizontal line. (f)~Share of the squared-distance discrepancy explained by successive maps. Marks in (c,~d,~f) are medians over pairs. Appendix~\ref{app:exp-s23} and Figure~\ref{fig:app-s21} give the details.}

caption_v6_archived.text: \caption{\textbf{Inside the premises of Theorem~\ref{thm:link}, InfoNCE and spectral learners come to agree exactly on the global order and keep a geometric gap that is the link of the theorem; CIFAR-5m networks outside these premises disagree on order criteria as well, and a monotone link removes little of what an affine map leaves.} Top row: the finite Gibbs model with certified empirical risk minimizers of both losses. (a) Share of pairs of runs whose global order $T_E$ of the distances among a fixed set of probe inputs agrees exactly, across the two objectives (filled circles) and within one objective (grey band, from the InfoNCE to the spectral value); the dashed curve and the dotted line give the agreement and the transition size $N^*$ predicted before the runs from the Gaussian limits of the two learners, that of InfoNCE given by Theorem~\ref{thm:peer}. (b) Kernel entries of one InfoNCE run against those of the spectral run with the same index at the largest sample size, on the axes and grey scale of (e), with the link of the theorem (dashed); the pair has the median difference after the link is undone (open squares of (c)) and was fixed before plotting. (c) Largest entrywise difference of the two distance matrices after each is divided by its mean (log scale, medians over pairs): across the objectives (filled circles), across them after the link is undone by applying its inverse to the spectral run (open squares), and within one objective (grey band, as in (a)); the dashed line marks the limit that the theorem predicts across the objectives, and the dotted segment the slope of $N^{-1/2}$. Bottom row: networks at $N=500{,}000$ images, with InfoNCE at temperature $0.2$. (d) Discrepancy between two runs divided by the frozen tolerance of each criterion: pairs within one objective (grey box, range), InfoNCE against the spectral loss (filled circles, medians), and an InfoNCE run against the exact link of the theorem applied to its own Gram matrix (diamonds; a positive control). Marks left of the vertical line lie within tolerance, and the theorem predicts disagreement above the horizontal line and agreement below it. (e) As (b) for the networks, with the best monotone link (solid); the pair is the median pair by the share of (f). (f) Median share of the squared-distance discrepancy explained by a common scale and then by an affine and a global monotone map (cross-fitted), for InfoNCE against the spectral loss (filled circles), for the positive control of (d) (diamonds), and for InfoNCE at $0.2$ against $0.5$ (open circles); the bar marks the share that the preregistered prediction required. Appendix~\ref{app:exp-s23} and Figure~\ref{fig:app-s21} give the details of the two rows.}
